dot:

The Commodore 64
A 1982 budget machine with 64 KB of RAM
that became a historic best-seller and cultural touchstone.
>];launch[label=<
1982: Launch
•  Named after its 64 KB RAM
•  Sept. 1, 1982 release date
•  First 64K computer to sell for under $600
•  August shipments made the launch date possible
•  Quality-control issues moved production to Kentron
>];success[label=<
Fast Success
•  Followed the VIC-20 and its proven market
•  Strong price/value vs. Atari 800XL
•  Atari supply problems made C-64 easier to find
•  500K sold in the first 6 months
•  5M by FY1984; ~10.6M C-64 units alone
•  ~12.3M including C-128
>];lasting[label=<
Why It Lasted
•  Right mix of compromises for the price
•  16 colors, 320x200 resolution, 8 sprites
•  Flexible 3-voice SID sound chip
•  Creative programmers kept extending it
•  ~700K/year into late 1980s
•  Still sold until 1993
>];impact[label=<
Human & Career Impact
•  Taught BASIC, 6502 assembly, and repairs
•  Many users entered IT careers
•  Not just games: homework, writing, data recovery
•  Reusing C-64 skills helped the author learn Python
>];legacy[label=<
Legacy
•  Helped inspire this retro-tech blog
•  Strong nostalgia for 12M+ former owners
•  2025 FPGA reissue sold ~19,000 units
•  Proved more than 30 years of staying power
>];title->launch;launch->success;success->lasting;lasting->impact;impact->legacy;}
